chapters: Royal Savile Row: Monarchs Who Ruled the Row
The Beaux on the Row: Men Who Led Fashion

title: The Italian Gentleman
creator: Hugo Jacomet

contents.scope: Contents and coverage only; no full book text.
contents.coverage: Profiles of more than fifty Italian houses, with mills and cloth merchants, bespoke tailors, sartorial brands, shirtmakers, ties/umbrellas/gloves and shoemakers. Examples include Vitale Barberis Canonico, Zegna, Rubinacci and Kiton.
contents.caveat: Use the detailed 2017 ISBN 9780500518571 listing. Slovart lists an inconsistent eight-section outline for the same ISBN, including Pitti Uomo; this is not merged into the six-part structure. The author says the book is a selected personal journey, not a complete catalog or academic history.

title: Suit shoulder expression: roped, natural, bald
creator: @classic_nonchalance (Cléa C.)
note: Episode 9 "Shoulders" of "How to be fluent in suits & tailoring in 48 lessons". Roped: sleeve head sits up and out. Natural: in between. Bald: relaxed and flat. Expression is shape, not construction; Spalla Camicia is a construction and can be roped, natural or bald. Roped does not mean padded; bald does not mean unconstructed. Names vary by tailor (e.g. "con rollino" in Rome). Built from burned-in captions and written caption only; audio not transcribed.

title: Journey to the End of the Night (1932)
creator: Louis-Ferdinand Céline
note: His first novel, called one of the masterpieces of 20th century French literature in the reel. Semi-autobiographical: follows Ferdinand Bardamu through World War I, colonial Africa, the United States and the poor suburbs of Paris.

title: Death on the Installment Plan (1936)
creator: Louis-Ferdinand Céline
note: The creator’s favorite: she loved it from the first pages. Semi-autobiographical, about his childhood growing up in the slums of Paris. Filled with hatred and disgust but also dreams and fantasies, and so visceral you can almost smell the dirtiness. Wikipedia lists the same 1936 novel as Death on Credit.

title: Round-table seating hierarchy
note: The reel places the seat of honour facing the entrance, for the host, highest-ranked guest or oldest person depending on occasion. Higher-status guests sit nearby, with rank decreasing farther away. Room orientation and proximity signal status; egalitarian design does not guarantee egalitarian behaviour. Creator dates Chinese round-table dining to the Tang dynasty and links yuan (round) to completeness/wholeness: these history/language claims are unchecked. Based on downloaded video audio, diagrams and caption. Creator says she is not an expert, and rigidity varies widely. Chapters 00:11 history; 00:27 hierarchies.

title: dqnamo's Kitchen
